Higashiyama-ku 63 places · area 1 of 9

Gion · Kiyomizu-dera · Sannenzaka · Kennin-ji · Yasaka · Tōfuku-ji

  1. 1 Must see within Higashiyama-ku · Wagashi

    Kagizen Yoshifusa (鍵善良房)

    A Gion institution since the early 18th century; its tea room is the classic place for kuzukiri.

    264 Gionmachi Kitagawa, Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto

    Recommended by , , +1,

  2. 2 Must see within Higashiyama-ku

    Kōdai-ji

    Founded 1606 by Nene in memory of Toyotomi Hideyoshi; a tsukiyama pond garden of man-made hills, pine and maple. Its sub-temple Entoku-in adds two more Zen gardens.

    Shimogawara-chō, Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by , ,

  3. 3 Must see within Higashiyama-ku

    Kiyomizu-dera

    Eastern Kyoto's hillside temple, famous for the wooden terrace with a view over the city; part of the UNESCO 'Historic Monuments of Ancient Kyoto'.

    Look for 06:00–18:00 (to 18:30 Jul–Aug); 500 yen

    Kiyomizu, Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by ,

  4. 4 Must see within Higashiyama-ku

    Higashiyama District (Sannenzaka & Ninenzaka)

    One of Kyoto's best-preserved historic districts — narrow lanes, wooden buildings and merchant shops on the 20–30 minute walk from Kiyomizu-dera to Yasaka Shrine.

    Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by ,

  5. 5 Must see within Higashiyama-ku

    Yasaka Shrine (Yasaka-jinja)

    Gion's great shrine, home of the Gion Matsuri every July for over a thousand years; busiest at cherry-blossom time beside Maruyama Park.

    Gionmachi, Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by ,

  6. 6 Must see within Higashiyama-ku

    Gion & Hanamikoji

    Kyoto's most famous geisha district, between Yasaka Shrine and the Kamo River — ochaya teahouses where geiko and maiko entertain.

    Gion, Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by ,

  7. 7 Must see within Higashiyama-ku

    Chion-in

    Head temple of the Jōdo (Pure Land) sect; its Sanmon, 24 m tall and 50 m wide, is the largest wooden temple gate in Japan (early 1600s).

    Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by ,

  8. 8 Must see within Higashiyama-ku

    Kennin-ji

    Founded 1202 — the oldest Zen temple in Kyoto, ranked third of the city's five great Zen temples, just south of Gion.

    Komatsu-chō (south of Gion), Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by ,

  9. 9 Must see within Higashiyama-ku

    Tōfuku-ji

    One of the Kyoto Gozan (five great Zen temples), founded in the 13th century; its Tsūten-kyō bridge over a maple valley is one of Kyoto's most famous autumn-leaf views.

    15-778 Honmachi, Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by ,

  10. 10 Must see within Higashiyama-ku

    Sanjūsangen-dō

    The 120-metre hall of 1266 (National Treasure) housing 1,001 standing Thousand-armed Kannon statues, flanked by Fūjin and Raijin.

    Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by ,

  11. 11 Must see within Higashiyama-ku · Soba

    Sōhonke Nishin Soba Matsuba

    Founded in 1861 as a theatre teahouse; in 1882 the second-generation owner invented nishin soba and moved beside the Minami-za kabuki theatre — the dish has been a Kyoto speciality ever since.

    Beside Minami-za, Shijō-dōri, Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by ,

  12. 12 Must see within Higashiyama-ku · Wagashi

    Gion Tokuya (ぎおん徳屋)

    Gion's warabi-mochi specialist — the melt-in-the-mouth real-bracken version, with a queue to match.

    Gion, Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto

    Recommended by ,

  13. 13 Must see within Higashiyama-ku · Sushi

    Gion Izuju (祇園 いづ重)

    A Kyō-zushi shop opposite Yasaka Shrine, founded in the late Meiji era by a former craftsman of Izuu who was given leave to open his own shop. Its saba-zushi uses true mackerel from the Sea of Japan.

    Gion, Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto (opposite Yasaka Shrine)

    Recommended by ,

  14. 14 Must see within Higashiyama-ku · Soba

    Gion Yorozuya

    Michelin Bib Gourmand udon house that began delivering meals to Gion teahouses and playhouses; queues form before opening for the onion udon heaped with Kyoto's Kujō spring onion.

    555-1 Komatsu-chō, Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto, Japan

    Recommended by

    Izuu

    367 Kiyomoto-chō, Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto 605-0084, Japan

    Kikunoi Honten

How we choose

Every place is recommended by named sources (review-aggregator star ratings never count as the recommender), pinned to its door from a published coordinate, and status-checked. Closed places stay, flagged, so you know they’re gone.

Must see
The places to plan a visit around — graded within each area, not across the city.
Worth the detour
Strong picks, worth going out of your way for.
Deep cut
For the curious: smaller, odder, more local.

Within each area, places are ordered by tier, then by number of named sources — never by popularity. Numbers on the cards match the pins on the map. No ratings, prices or opening hours are shown, because the guide doesn’t hold verified ones.

215 sights and 183 places to eat across Kyoto and its day-trip ring, every one traceable to its source: the seventeen UNESCO Historic Monuments of Ancient Kyoto and Nara's World Heritage temples, Gion and Pontochō, Arashiyama and Ōhara, Michelin-starred kaiseki and Bib Gourmand soba, saba-zushi and eel, Uji tea and the Fushimi sake district.

How this guide was made

How the cuisine filters were policed

Every food card names a specific dish — a label alone doesn’t qualify. A cuisine tag names the kitchen’s own tradition, never one dish it serves. Tabelog and Retty scores may measure popularity but never count as a source.

Web-searched in Japanese and English, fact-checked

Every place is traceable to two credible sources, or a lone Michelin / UNESCO / Agency for Cultural Affairs designation — recorded in data/sources.json. Every coordinate is verified into data/geocodes.json and every place status-checked open. Yelp/TripAdvisor/Tabelog never count toward the two-source bar.
